## Summary

The tweet: **"if you build trend-following systems, bookmark this and run the same 6 tests on yours. it might save you from trading a lucky backtest."**

The chart (attached photo, OCR'd) shows the one test visible to us — **Execution & Cost Stress Testing**: cumulative equity curves 2000–~2028 for the same trend system under degraded execution:

| Variant | Assumptions | Final equity |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 1 bps slippage + $0.005/sh comm | $7.27M |
| 2x costs | 2 bps + $0.010/sh | $7.18M |
| 3x costs | 3 bps + $0.015/sh | ~$7.08M |
| 5x costs | 5 bps + $0.025/sh | $6.61M |
| 10x costs | 10 bps + $0.050/sh | $5.18M |
| 1-day execution lag | delay 1d | $6.73M |
| 2-day execution lag | delay 2d | $7.58M |

Read: the edge degrades **gracefully and monotonically** under cost inflation (10x costs still compounds, −29%), and — the striking wrinkle — **lag is not monotonic**: 1d lag costs more than 5x costs do, yet 2d lag ends *above* baseline ($7.58M). For a slow trend system, a day or two of execution delay is noise around the signal, not death; transaction costs are the real tax. A "lucky backtest" is one that needs the 1 bps / zero-lag fairy tale to work.

The other 5 of the 6 tests are inside the X article (login-gated at capture) — not yet read, not guessed at here.

## Why it matters

We keep a live line of systematic strategies in this vault — [[2026-08-29-three-simple-ma-atr-systems]], [[2026-08-30-ignis-trend-following-realtest]], the milk-man series ([[2026-09-01-milk-man-backtest-notional-normalization]] and forward) — and the failure mode this tweet warns about (edge that evaporates under realistic friction) is exactly the gap between a pretty curve and a tradeable one. The cost-grid is mechanical to implement in RealTest/our backtest harness: rerun the same config at 2x/3x/5x/10x friction and with a 1–2 bar execution delay, and look for graceful degradation rather than collapse.

Skepticism gates: single chart from one demo system — the dollar figures are his, not ours; universe/period parameters beyond the 2000–~2028 axis are unknown; social-proof stats weren't exposed at capture; and 5 of the 6 tests remain unread behind the login wall, so this note captures the *method demonstrated*, not the full checklist.
